title: model-identity-data: names language models choose for themselves (exploratory release)
description:
Aggregate results of an exploratory study of the names that language models choose when asked to name themselves. 84 models from 20 families (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT and gpt-oss, DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu GLM, OLMo, Google Gemma, Mistral and two community tunings of Mistral 7B, Baidu ERNIE, TII Falcon, IBM Granite, Hugging Face SmolLM, NVIDIA Nemotron, Phi, OpenAssistant, Inception Mercury (diffusion language models), and Pythia and GPT-2 as pre-chat comparisons) answered 40 self-naming prompts and 40 matched control prompts (names for a pet, a baby, a fictional character, a robot), 40 samples each, plus prompt sets varying framing, system message, temperature, language and answer format: 736,408 answers, and 16,394 answers to a follow-up asking why the name was chosen. For 49 open models and 8 training checkpoints, the probabilities of candidate names after an AI-naming and a pet-naming context are also reported.

Version 1.3.0 adds 11 models (Qwen2.5-14B base and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, gpt-oss-20b, Phi-4-reasoning, Falcon 7B base and instruct, ERNIE 4.5 base and chat, Inception Mercury 2, 2.5 and 3), an answer category for a provider's content filter, thinking on vs off for R1-Distill and Mercury, an answer-parser update and an updated paper; no planned-test outcome changed. See the end of REPORT.md.

Contents: a findings report, aggregate CSV tables with a data dictionary, figures, the exact prompts, and a paper (LaTeX source and PDF). No full answers, reasoning texts or per-answer records are included; the tables list the short name string parsed from each answer.

Status: exploratory. The data were collected without a frozen pre-registration; results are descriptive and should be treated as hypotheses.
notes: Exploratory release. Planned hypothesis tests were run on these data and are reported as descriptive results.
